sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: The S&P 500 sits at 7,805, up about 2.4% over the past month and roughly 0.2% below its 1-month high. The Nasdaq 100 is at 30,569, up about 5.0% over the same stretch but still about 2.1% under its high. VIX has eased to 15.3 from 17.1 a month ago, while the Euro Stoxx 50 is slightly lower over the month at 6,167. The week brings 148 scheduled reports from S&P 500, Russell 1000 and portfolio names, with the heaviest days Wednesday (48) and Thursday (49), and financial-services and industrials the largest groups.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Tuesday: HAL US and WFRD US report into the oil-gas cluster, which sits at a -2.7% median reaction. Wednesday: TXN US, LRCX US and IBM US report in technology, median +1.25%. Thursday: BX US reports as the main name in alternative asset management, median +2.9% off recent prints, and VLO US adds to the oil-gas group. Friday: SLB US closes out the energy services names in the week.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Three sectors lead the reaction table: mining (+6.6% median across 178 tickers), alternative asset management (+2.9%, 6 tickers) and oil-gas (-2.7%, 33 tickers). Mining carries the largest ticker base; the other two are smaller samples, so read them with that in mind.
